## Day 1

Take [this data](https://austin-cutler.quarto.pub/summer-ri-workshop/class_toy_data.csv) and clean it in the following ways. These steps do not need to be completed in order, as long as they are all completed.

1. Make sure the variable names are correct and that the variables are formatted properly—that is, numeric variables are read as numeric and character variables are read as characters.

   **Hint:** Look at the documentation for the function you are using to read the data by entering `?read_csv` in the console.

2. Using `select()`, make a new data frame containing only the following variables: Age, Gender, Income, Approval Rating, Political Party, Opinion Text, Gun Control, and Abortion.

3. At least one variable has negative numbers where the values should be read as `NA`. Find that variable and replace its negative values.

   This involves `case_when()` and `mutate()`, which we discussed in class.




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="true" code-summary="Show Hint"}
# Make sure to include TRUE ~ x. This keeps the variable unchanged
# in all other instances.
data %>%
  mutate(
    x = case_when(
      x < 0 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE  ~ x
    )
  )
```
:::




4. Leave only Republicans in the data. Remember the `filter()` function.

5. Upload your cleaned data and your code [here](https://www.dropbox.com/request/HHDxOiVqwY0Jitv8U5og). Use `write_csv()` and name the file `lastname_hw1_data.csv`.

```r
library(tidyverse)

data %>%
  mutate(doing_some_data_cleaning_here) %>%
  select(the_variables_I_want) %>%
  filter(the_observations_I_want) -> data

write_csv(
  data,
  "path/where/you/want/it/saved/lastname_hw1_data.csv"
)
```

## Day 2

1. Download one of the datasets from the [Data](data.qmd) page and load it into R. It can be any dataset you want; the available choices are meant to represent a range of interests. If you would rather use a different dataset, send me an email.

2. Make a tidy data frame:

   - Pull out only the variables that interest you. These can include variables that do not appear directly in a figure or analysis but identify observations.
   - Use the codebook to identify values representing missing data and remove those values.

3. Practice using `group_by()` and `summarize()`:

   - Identify two categorical variables of interest.
   - Calculate group size with `n()`.
   - Calculate the group mean of two continuous variables.

```r
# Roughly what your code should look like for each calculation:
data %>%
  group_by(categorical_variable) %>%
  summarize(average = mean(continuous_variable))
```

4. Get the number of rows and columns in the cleaned version of your data.

5. Report summary statistics for the continuous variables in your data.

Upload your homework [here](https://www.dropbox.com/request/k7GKmpdAUNlKDv9yFD0n).
